title: Partially Identified Ambiguity
abstract: arXiv:2602.07634v3 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: This paper addresses the normative question of whether one should condition on the data when performing robust Bayesian analysis under partial identification. We provide an ex ante representation of the conditional Gamma-minimax criterion and show that it can violate Aumann plausibility, a set-valued generalization of the rational expectations property. Our main characterization result establishes that Aumann plausibility holds if and only if the decision maker's prior set exhibits partially identified ambiguity. The latter condition requires the prior set to equal the Aumann expectation of a random set of distributions supported on the parameter's identified sets. We interpret these results as suggesting that conditional Gamma-minimax should only be used under partially identified ambiguity. The implications for various robust Bayesian methods are discussed.

tldr: 本文刻画了条件Gamma-极小极大准则满足Aumann合理性的充要条件——决策者的先验集合须呈现“部分识别模糊性”，并据此主张该准则仅在部分识别模糊性下才应使用。
